description: Comprehensive taxonomy and schema of ancient Indian sound philosophy, Nāda Brahma, Āhata/Anāhata classification, vocal/body acoustics (Śarīrotpatti), and metaphysical musicology grounded in classical treatises.
source_treatises_referenced: Sangita Ratnakara (Sarangadeva, 1230 AD) - Pindotpatti & Nada-Svara Prakarana
Natya Shastra (Bharata Muni, c. 200 BC) - Atodhya & Sharira Vidhi
Brihaddesi (Matanga Muni, c. 800 AD) - Nada Tattva Lakshana
The Ragas of Karnatic Music (N.S. Ramachandran, 1938 AD)

etymology_and_definition.root_derivation: Derived from "nadyate" (that which vibrates/manifests) or the combination of "Na" (Prāṇa / Vital Air) and "Da" (Anala / Agni / Cosmic Fire).
etymology_and_definition.core_doctrine: Sound is not merely physical vibration but the primal creative energy of the universe (Nāda Brahma) and the ultimate vehicle for spiritual liberation (Nādopāsanā).
etymology_and_definition.shloka_ref: Nakaram prananamanamanalam nakaram viduh | Jatah prananala-samyogad tasmad nado'dhibhiyate || (Sangita Ratnakara)

anahata_nada.title: Anāhatā Nāda (Unstruck Cosmic Vibration)
anahata_nada.description: The uncreated, eternal sound heard by enlightened yogis in deep meditation without physical friction or impact. It resides in the Anāhata Chakra and is the goal of Nādopāsanā.
anahata_nada.audibility: Inaudible to normal human ears; experienced in Samādhi.
anahata_nada.metaphysical_significance: Cosmic resonance of Brahman, free from decay or cause.

ahata_nada.title: Āhatā Nāda (Struck Audible Vibration)
ahata_nada.description: Sound generated through physical friction, impact, or vibration of air. It forms the entire basis of music, vocalization, speech, and instrumental performance.
ahata_nada.audibility: Audible to human ears with a specific, sustained frequency (musical tone).

five_sources_classification.description: Produced by the human vocal apparatus through prāṇa (breath) passing through the throat and head cavities.
Produced by wooden stringed or wind instruments (e.g. Vīṇā, Flute).
Produced by metallic instruments or cymbals (e.g. Tāḷam, Cymbals, Gongs).
Produced by stretched animal skin or percussion membranes (e.g. Mṛdaṅgam, Kanjira).
Produced by column of air vibrating inside a pipe or wind instrument (e.g. Nāgasvaram, Flute).

sarirotpatti_five_stages_of_nada.name: Ati-Sūkṣma (Ultra-subtle)
sarirotpatti_five_stages_of_nada.description: The initial subtle spark of sound arising at the base of the spine.

sarirotpatti_five_stages_of_nada.name: Sūkṣma (Subtle)
sarirotpatti_five_stages_of_nada.description: The swelling of subtle sound as breath rises through the abdomen.

sarirotpatti_five_stages_of_nada.name: Puṣṭa (Developed / Manifesting)
sarirotpatti_five_stages_of_nada.description: The acoustic resonance taking shape in the chest register (Mandra Sthāyī).

sarirotpatti_five_stages_of_nada.name: Apuṣṭa (Unrefined Manifestation)
sarirotpatti_five_stages_of_nada.description: Sound emerging in the throat register (Madhya Sthāyī) where swaras get articulated.

sarirotpatti_five_stages_of_nada.name: Kṛtrimā / Vyakta (Articulate / Musical Sound)
sarirotpatti_five_stages_of_nada.description: Fully realized musical sound and speech passing through the oral cavity and head register (Tāra Sthāyī).

three_sthayis_and_body_registers.acoustic_quality: Balanced, clear, natural singing pitch range.

nadopasana.description: Treating music not merely as entertainment (Rañjana) but as a spiritual Sādhanā to achieve Mokṣa (liberation), as taught by Saint Purandara Dāsa and Saint Tyāgarāja (e.g. in kṛtis like "Nāda Tanumanusam", "Nādōpāsanā").

svara_ranjakatva.definition: Swato ranjayati srotruchittanam sa swarochyate - A swara is that which inherently pleases and elevates the soul of the listener on its own.

panca_bhuta_sound_mapping.principle: Medium of Nāda; pure unmanifested space.
Movement of breath (Prāṇa) creating wave vibration.
Heat and mental will (Icchā Śakti) driving sound generation.
Fluidity and continuity of Gamaka glides.
